In the late 1960s, Elliott relocated to Los Angeles to pursue a career in acting, which his father had dissuaded him from doing, instead urging him to obtain a college degree.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-baker-3) "He gave me that proverbial line, 'You've got a snowball's chance in hell of having a career in (Hollywood),'" Elliott recalled. "He was a realist, my dad. He was a hard worker. He had a work ethic that I've fashioned mine after, and I thank him for that every day."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-baker-3) Elliott worked in construction while studying acting and served in the California Air National Guard's 146th Airlift Wing (the Hollywood Guard) at Van Nuys Airport before the unit moved to Channel Islands Air National Guard Station in 1990.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-11)
Elliott with Juliet Mills in _Once an Eagle_ (1976)
Elliott in his breakthrough role in _Lifeguard_ (1976)
Elliott began his career as a character actor; his appearance, voice, and bearing were well-suited to Westerns. In 1969, he earned his first television credit as Dan Kenyon in _Judd, for the Defense_ in the episode "The Crystal Maze".
texts.6: That same year he appeared in the show _Lancer_ in the episode "Death Bait", playing Renslo.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-complete-12) He went on to appear in two additional episodes of the series between 1970 and 1971.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-complete-12) One of his early film roles was as a card player who watches as the Sundance Kid (Robert Redford) demonstrates his shooting ability in the opening scene of _Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid_ (1969).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-tvg-13) In the 1970–1971 television season, Elliott starred as Doug Robert for several episodes in the hit series _Mission: Impossible_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-tvg-13) Beginning in 1972, Elliott appeared as the cowboy Walker in a series of Falstaff Beer commercials.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-16) In 1975, Elliott was cast in a lead role as Charles Wood in the television film _I Will Fight No More Forever_, a dramatization of Chief Joseph's resistance to the U.S. government's forcible removal of his Nez Perce Indian tribe to a reservation in Idaho.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-17)
texts.7: From 1976 to 1977, he played the lead character Sam Damon in the miniseries _Once an Eagle_, an adaptation of the Anton Myrernovel of the same name, opposite Amy Irving, Kim Hunter, Clu Gulager, and Melanie Griffith.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-18) He also had a starring role as Rick Carlson in the summer sleeper hit _Lifeguard_ (1976), which marked his feature film breakthrough.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-davis-19) He portrayed a lifeguard in Southern California who reevaluates his life choices after being invited to a reunion.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-lgv-20)_Variety_ deemed the film "unsatisfying," adding: "Elliott, who has some beefcake value, projects a character who is mostly a passive reactor rather than a person in sure command of his fate."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-lgv-20)
texts.8:
### Recognition as a character actor
[edit]
Elliott in _Aspen_ (1977)
Elliott played Tom Keating in the TV miniseries _Aspen_ in 1977. He later played an abusive wife-killer in the made-for-TV movie _Murder in Texas_ (1981) opposite Farrah Fawcett and his future wife Katharine Ross,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-21) and starred with Cheryl Ladd in the TV miniseries _A Death in California_ (1985).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-22) In 1979, he co-starred with Tom Selleck in the popular miniseries adaptation of [Louis L'Amour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_L'Amour "Louis L'Amour")'s _The Sacketts_. Elliott and Selleck were a team again in 1982 in _The Shadow Riders_, another Louis L'Amour adaption.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-match-23)
Elliott had a supporting role in _Mask_ (1985) opposite Cher. He played a hard-nosed, rough-around-the-edges but ultimately sympathetic father figure in the Christmas film _Prancer_ (1989). He has made guest appearances on shows including _The Felony Squad_, _Gunsmoke_, _Lancer_, and _Hawaii Five-O_, and has been featured in many TV movies, including _Buffalo Girls_ (1995), in which he played Wild Bill Hickok.
texts.9:
### Recognition as a character actor
In 1986, he starred in the TV movie _Gone to Texas_, based on a biography of Sam Houston. The role allowed him to play Houston as both fighter and a man who grew into a skillful political leader; the film depicted his disgrace as governor of Tennessee, his return to his Cherokee Nation friends, and his pivotal role in the liberation of Texas from Mexico in 1836. Elliott appeared with Patrick Swayze in _Road House_ (1989) as Wade Garrett, a bouncer, mentor and friend of Swayze's character. In 1991, Elliott and his wife Katharine Ross starred in the adaptation of the [Louis L'Amour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_L'Amour "Louis L'Amour") novel _Conagher_ (1991).[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-24)
He portrayed Brigadier GeneralJohn Buford in the 1993 historical drama _Gettysburg_, and the same year played Virgil Earp in the Western _Tombstone_ (1993).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-afi-25) Elliott played The Stranger, a character narrating the story of _The Big Lebowski_ (1998).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-afi-25) He co-starred in _We Were Soldiers_ (2002), an adaptation of _We Were Soldiers Once… And Young_, in which he portrayed Command Sergeant MajorBasil L. Plumley. He played General Thaddeus Ross in the 2003 action film _Hulk_.
In 2005, he appeared in _Thank You for Smoking_ as a former Marlboro Man advertisement cowboy who has developed lung cancer. In 2006 he provided the voice for the character Ben the Cow in the animated film _Barnyard_.
texts.10:
### Recognition as a character actor
In 2007, Elliott joined the comic book adaptation _Ghost Rider_. He played the character Carter Slade. The same year, Elliott appeared in _The Golden Compass_ as the character Lee Scoresby. The film is based on _Northern Lights_ in Philip Pullman's trilogy _His Dark Materials_. Also appearing in the film are Nicole Kidman, Christopher Lee, and Daniel Craig.
In 2009, Elliott had a small role in _Up In The Air_ in which he portrayed the chief pilot of American Airlines. He appeared three times on _Parks and Recreation_ as Ron Dunn, the Eagleton equivalent of Ron Swanson; Dunn is a hippie, compared to Swanson's staunch survivalist and Libertarian personality. He then provided the voice of Buster (a.k.a. Chupadogra) in the animated film _Marmaduke_ (2010). He had a supporting role in the thriller film _The Company You Keep_ and played a college football coach in 2014's drama film _Draft Day_.
Elliott and Jon Hamm at the 2017 Sundance Film Festival
texts.11:
### Recognition as a character actor
In 2015, Elliott appeared opposite Lily Tomlin as a former love interest of a grandmother (Tomlin) attempting to help her pregnant granddaughter in Paul Weitz's comedy _Grandma_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-NYTimes-Gma-AnatomyScene-2015-26) In the same year he appeared in the romance _[I'll See You in My Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'll\_See\_You\_in\_My\_Dreams\_(2015\_film) "I'll See You in My Dreams (2015 film)")_, and had a role in the independent film _Digging for Fire_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-NYTimes-SamElliott-LeadingMan-2015-27) In 2015, he won the [Critics' Choice Television Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Choice_Television_Award "Critics' Choice Television Award") for best guest performer in a drama for his role in the FX Network's show _Justified_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-NYTimes-SamElliott-LeadingMan-2015-27)
texts.12:
### Career resurgence and critical acclaim
[edit]
In 2015, Elliott began appearing as a series regular in the Netflix series _The Ranch_, opposite Ashton Kutcher and Danny Masterson.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-28) He also had a recurring role as Phil Millstein in the second season of _Grace and Frankie_. In film, he supplied the voice of Butch in the animated film _The Good Dinosaur_ (2015).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-TGD-Recast-29)
In 2017, Elliott starred in _The Hero_, as Lee Hayden, an aging Western icon with a golden voice, whose best performances are decades behind him.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-30) His work in the film received much critical acclaim with Joey Magidson, writing for _AwardsCircuit_, proclaiming that "Elliott is perfect here. _The Hero_ encapsulates everything you love about him into one package."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-31) Later that year, Elliott starred in _The Man Who Killed Hitler and Then the Bigfoot_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-32)
texts.13:
### Career resurgence and critical acclaim
The following year, Elliott costarred in _A Star Is Born_ (2018), in which he plays Bobby Maine, the elder half-brother of Bradley Cooper's lead character.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-33) Elliott received critical acclaim for his performance, winning the National Board of Review Award for Best Supporting Actor.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-nbr-34) He was also nominated for the Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Supporting Role, as well as the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor, his career-first nomination.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-35) Commenting on his Academy Award nomination, Elliott declared: "I think the thing off the top of my head might be, 'It's about fucking time!'"[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-36) Since 2019, he played Wild West, new Mayor of Quahog, in 21 episodes of the animated series Family Guy. Wild West is a parody of Western film characters.
In 2022, Elliott starred as Shea Brennan on the Paramount+ miniseries _1883_, a prequel to the _Yellowstone_ series. The show's story involves Brennan as he leads a group of immigrants from Fort Worth, Texas into the untamed western areas of the plains, and its connection to the Dutton family and its migration to Montana. The show aired from late 2021 until February 2022. For his performance he received critical acclaim and won the Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Miniseries or Television Movie.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-37)
In 2025, Elliott starred in the second season of the Paramount+ series _Landman_, as T. L. Norris, the father of the Billy Bob Thornton's lead character.
texts.14:
### Career resurgence and critical acclaim
In 1998, Elliott was named the grand marshal of the Calgary Stampede parade and rode in the procession before an estimated 300,000 spectators.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-38)
